subject: Deployment-mode implications: logs, KMS, backups and data isolation

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + a couple follow-ups from today's demo

Hi Emily — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Appreciate you walking us through the integration goals for the EHR connector and the constraints around PHI. A quick recap and the two items we promised to confirm: 

- Priority needs you called out: absolute separation of customer data from other tenants, no long-lived plaintext snapshots outside your control, and centralized KMS where keys are customer-managed.
- You said preferred deployment was either Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) depending on backup & control-plane guarantees.

Follow-ups we promised: 
1) Clarify how backups and VM/snapshot artifacts are handled in Dedicated vs Private. Are customer snapshots persisted to a customer-owned storage bucket (or accessible for retrieval by your team) or are they retained on vendor-managed storage?
2) Confirm the control-plane connectivity model for Private: is there a requirement for air-gapped install, or is a customer-managed control plane with routed telemetry acceptable?

I've attached a compact deployment matrix that contrasts where logs, snapshots, and KMS live per deployment mode. See attachment: Redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx (XLSX) and our SOC2 summary for audit posture: SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF).

Next steps I propose: I can loop in our security/ops SME to answer the backup/snapshot details — tagging @Karthik for the exact behavior, and @Kimberly to coordinate any procurement/security artifacts. Are you available for a 30-min follow-up on Wednesday 5/21 10:00–10:30 PT?

Thanks,
Markus Klein

Hi team — answering inline with concise calls-to-action so Markus can share ahead of the 10:00 PT sync.

1) Dedicated snapshots/backups:
- Behavior: By default, Dedicated instances run on Redwood-managed compute but snapshots of instance disks and model caches are written to Redwood-managed object storage to enable fast failover and redeploys. Those artifacts are encrypted at rest using envelope encryption.
- BYOK: We can support a customer-managed KMS key for envelope keys when customers sign an enterprise agreement and choose a Dedicated+ (reserved capacity with customer KMS) option. That causes snapshot metadata to be wrapped with your key; raw objects remain in Redwood-managed buckets but are unreadable without your key.
- Retention & export: Retention is configurable per-contract; we can configure daily retention windows and provide a one-time export to a customer-owned bucket for longer term archival as part of onboarding. Action: Kimberly to include contract clause language (we have precedent language — I'll attach).

2) Private (VPC / on-prem) behaviors:
- If you deploy Private in your VPC (Redwood-managed control plane with private peering) or fully on-premises, snapshots and model caches can be written to customer-owned storage in your VPC (S3) or on-prem artifact stores — i.e., no Redwood-managed bucket required.
- BYOK/HSM: For Private we support BYOK with HSM-backed keys for both control-plane metadata and serving-level encryption. For on-prem, the HSM can be customer-provided or integrated with an approved HSM vendor. Action: Karthik to prepare the ops checklist for HSM integration steps & network requirements.

3) Logs & telemetry:
- Splunk/SIEM: We have two options: push mode (we forward sanitized control-plane audit logs to a customer collector over an encrypted channel) or pull mode (customer pulls via secure API).
- Redaction: We do not include full model inputs/outputs in control-plane audit logs by default. Inputs/outputs are stored in a separate, opt-in telemetry store for debugging; that store is disabled unless you opt in and explicitly grant access. For standard control-plane logs we include operation ids, timestamps, routing decisions, and error traces — no payloads. Action: Kimberly to attach a log schema and a sample sanitized audit log entry for Emily/security to review.

Summary (to share with Emily before Wed 10:00 PT):
- Dedicated: snapshots live on Redwood-managed buckets by default, encrypted; BYOK is supported under Enterprise Dedicated+ with envelope wrapping; we can export artifacts to your bucket on onboarding.
- Private: snapshots can be written to your storage; BYOK/HSM supported for serving and control-plane.
- Logs: supported Splunk forwarder / API; default logs are payload-free; opt-in telemetry store holds inputs/outputs and is disabled unless requested.

I'll attach the contract clause template, ops HSM checklist, and a sample sanitized audit log. Markus — want me to drop these in the HubSpot deal record now?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
